concepts.def: Method evaluating environmental impacts of a product across its life from raw materials to disposal, standardised in ISO 14040.
Lifecycle analysis covering all stages from raw material extraction through manufacture, use and final disposal.
Design philosophy by McDonough and Braungart (2002) where end-of-life materials become inputs for new products.
Total energy required to produce a material or product, including extraction, processing and transport.
Total greenhouse gas emissions caused directly and indirectly by a product, person or organisation, measured in CO2 equivalents.
Sustainability framework: Rethink, Refuse, Reduce, Reuse, Repair and Recycle, guiding designers towards lower-impact products.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Sustainability & Ethics — a core area of A-Level Design Technology.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Sustainability & Ethics brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Sustainability & Ethics.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Why do designers often use 5th to 95th percentile data instead of just the 50th?
options: Because the 50th percentile is too unreliable.
It stays constant.
Because law requires it.
